newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BUDGET DEF TO OVERSHOOT TARGET IN 97 - EIU.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BUDGET DEF TO OVERSHOOT TARGET IN 97 - EIU.

text.p: Greece is likely to overshoot its 1996 budget target of 7.6 percent of GDP and will miss its 1997 deficit gaol of 4.2 percent of GDP by two percentage points due to higher that projected salaries, the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) said in its latest report on Greece.

"Although measures to reduce expenditure, supplemented by some revenue increases, are envisaged, the expected laxity over salaries will slow the reduction in the general government deficit. The actual deficit in 1997 will be 2.0 perentage points higher than the 4.2 percent target," it said.
The government will have to impose a severe budget in 1998 that will reduce the deficit to 4.5 percent of GDP, said the EIU report.

The EIU predicted that higher than expected wages would also hinder the fast deceleration in inflation despite the countervailing influence of the drachma which will lead to a wider current account deficit. Inflation is forecast to average 8.6 percet in 1996, 7.5 percent in 1997 and 6.5 percent in 1996.

The average rate on the 12-month T-bill will be at 13.2 percent in 1996 versus a projected 12.0 percent in 1997 and 10 percent in 1998, it said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
